ops.title: ccp add hangs on File Provider: private .claude.json must be seeded before Setup's readiness probe
ops.body:
## Symptom
`ccp add` for a File Provider account hangs (6+ min) then fails: `file provider setup <dir>: file provider domain did not serve an enumeration in time: acct-NN`. Every retry leaves an orphan registered domain with no backing that floods the daemon log with `open acct-NN.private/.claude.json: no such file`.

## Root cause (ordering bug)
`Manager.PrepareAdd` calls `prov.Setup()` (account.go) which, for File Provider, registers the domain AND runs `waitDomainServes` (fusekit overlay/provider.go) — a readiness poll of the app's ProbeDomain that reads `.claude.json` through the content bridge. But `PrepareAdd` seeds the private `.claude.json` only AFTER Setup. So the probe reads a `.claude.json` that doesn't exist yet.

`waitDomainServes` says a missing `.claude.json` (nil byte-count) SHOULD count as serving — but `PoolContentSource.ReadSynth` (contentsource.go:~102) returns a hard ERROR on a missing private `.claude.json` ("read private claude.json for %s"), on the assumption "a seeded fuse account always has a private file." That holds for fuse (private file swept in before the mount) but NOT for File Provider, whose domain serves during Setup, before the seed. The error → ProbeDomain reports not-serving → readiness times out. Symlink/fuse have no readiness probe, so the seed-after-Setup order never mattered; acct-13 was the first FP add under v0.45.0's readiness-gated Setup.

## Fix (cc-pool v0.45.3)
In `PrepareAdd`, for `BackendFileProvider` only, `MkdirAll(prov.PrivateRoot(dir))` + `seedClaudeJSON` BEFORE `prov.Setup()`, so the fresh domain can serve `.claude.json` at probe time. FP has no fuse-style fallback, so no re-seed dance. The existing post-Setup seed stays (idempotent for FP: re-reads the stripped seed, no oauthAccount → re-seeds). Test: `TestPrepareAddFileProviderSeedsBeforeSetup` (stub Setup fails if the private file is absent). Did NOT touch ReadSynth's deliberate error-on-missing (avoids masking genuine fuse corruption / leaking base identity).

## Recover an already-broken account (orphan domain)
`ccp fp repair` needs a DB row, so it can't reap the orphan. Deregister directly via the companion app control socket: `fileproviderd.NewAppClient(pool.FPControlSocketPath()).Remove(ctx, "acct-NN")` (domain id = filepath.Base(configDir)); OpRemove is idempotent. Then remove leftover `acct-NN.private/`. Confirm the fix by seeding `acct-NN.private/.claude.json` (oauthAccount stripped) → the ENOENT flood stops and the domain serves.

## Related (separate bugs seen same session)
- daemon restart drops the FP companion app and doesn't re-ensure it (on-demand spawn only) → `domains.sock` refused; relaunch: `open -g /Applications/CCPoolStatus.app`.
- orphan FP domains are never reaped by the daemon (P1c gap) — each failed add leaks one.
ops.when: ccp add on a File Provider account hangs/times out with 'file provider domain did not serve an enumeration in time'; or working on PrepareAdd, the FP Setup readiness probe, or PoolContentSource.ReadSynth
